svg.title: A timeout is not a failure: after
svg.desc: Checkout A holds seats A12 and A13 in a short transaction that commits at once, then calls the payment provider with no transaction open. The read timeout fires before the provider answers, so checkout records the payment as UNKNOWN in a second short transaction and answers 202 Accepted while the seats stay held. The provider charges the card a moment later. The reconciliation job then asks the provider for the status of the charge by its idempotency key, learns that the card was charged, confirms the order, and sells the seats.
svg.text: After: record UNKNOWN, then ask by idempotency key
The timeout becomes an UNKNOWN payment in a short transaction, and reconciliation settles it with a status query.

g.text: throws if a caller's transaction is open
held for A, committed, not locked
The timeout became an UNKNOWN payment, and the seats stayed held for A.
A status query by idempotency key found the charge, and reconciliation confirmed the order.

svg.text: Sources: quarkus.io/guides/transaction (declarative and programmatic), quarkus.io/guides/rest-client (read timeout), and quarkus.io/guides/scheduler.
